roiCoordinateStatus: All four R1 polygons fit 1920×1080 bounds. They describe reception areas, not individual chair IDs; original authoring dimensions are unrecorded.
notes: Three double counters and one single counter are inferred from four overlapping views. Seven staff chairs are provisional workstation positions.
All Seat_SGS_TMP_* IDs are local temporary IDs; no G32 chair/table ROI mapping was found. Review chair counts and IDs before telemetry integration.
Stone-and-teal counter fronts, wood worktops/back panels, dark office chairs and two end luggage scales are supported by the snapshots. Dimensions remain estimated.
SGSCam1 and SGSCam3 share the flyadeal display/counter; SGSCam2 and SGSCam4 show the staff side. Their repeated workstations are modeled once.
Local axes follow the counter row. Full-floor alignment and camera calibration remain unresolved; registered camera coordinates were preserved.
Owner approved the basic G32 arrangement; all 32 original objects and their transforms, finishes and temporary seat identities are unchanged.

All four normal/wide pairs and the ground-floor SGS map crop were reviewed for permanent surroundings. Four kiosks, third scale, exit details and four schematic counter notices bring the editable inventory to 44 objects.
Opposite kiosk wall and approach wall are provisional local surrounding context, not accepted global boundaries. Adjacent reception and security equipment remain unmodeled.

Exposed stored materials in wide views are temporary per owner and are excluded, including loose decorative fixtures and additional stored chairs. Normal-image ROI coordinates are never applied to wide frames.
Floor-map topology supports the established four banks; it does not measure the expanded shell. Glass motif, sill heights, door hardware and kiosk positions remain approximate.

Latest owner clarification restores a solid wall section and more floor space beyond the exit on the left. The added 1.2 m allowance is provisional; full-side patterned glass is retained and extends with the wall. This supersedes the prior door-at-corner alignment.
